Beyond the glass a dogfight rages — enemy fighters streak past trailing tracer fire, a ship erupting in a silent blossom of flame against the starfield.
Beyond the canopy a colossal banded planet looms huge on approach, its atmosphere glowing along the limb, a moon hanging beyond it.
Beyond the glass the lit mouth of a docking bay yawns open ahead, guide-lights strobing, the dark hull of a station filling the view around it.
Beyond the canopy a glowing nebula fills everything — vast curtains of violet and gold gas stretching horizon to horizon, young stars burning inside the clouds.
Beyond the glass an asteroid field tumbles ahead, boulders the size of cities turning slowly, gaps threaded by light, collision shadows flickering across the canopy.
Beyond the canopy a colossal capital ship slides past, its hull a city of running lights and gun turrets, so close its plating fills the entire view.
Beyond the glass a jump-point swirls ahead — a disc of churning blue-white light tearing open space, its edges crackling with arcing energy discharge.
Beyond the canopy a blazing sun sits low and enormous ahead, its corona writhing, the instrument panel lit gold, solar flares arcing silently off the limb.
Beyond the glass a fleet moves in tight formation — dozens of warships arrayed in echelon, engine trails painting parallel lines across the dark, their running lights blinking in unison.
Beyond the canopy a deep-space station hangs ahead, its ring structure slowly rotating, dock arms extending, a constellation of smaller craft orbiting it like moths.
Beyond the glass a starfield stretches deep and still, a distant world visible as a pale blue point of light, its moon a faint companion beside it.
Beyond the canopy a debris field drifts — twisted hull sections, shattered gun emplacements, a cracked viewport still lit from inside, everything tumbling in slow silent ruin.
Beyond the glass two enemy fighters close in fast from the left, cannon fire stitching white lines through the dark, a third exploding in a rolling orange fireball.
Beyond the canopy an ice giant rises below the nose, its rings cutting a sharp shadow line, a shepherd moon threading the gap at tremendous speed.
Beyond the glass a derelict freighter drifts broadside ahead, its cargo pods blown open, contents scattering in a glittering slow cloud across the starfield.
Beyond the canopy a binary star system fills the view — two suns in close orbit pulling a bridge of plasma between them, the light hard and shifting.
Beyond the glass a planetary ring plane stretches flat to the horizon, ice particles catching sunlight like a road of broken mirrors stretching away forever.
Beyond the canopy a battle-carrier launches fighters in rapid sequence, each one flung down the rail and gone in a streak, the bay cycling with mechanical urgency.
Beyond the glass a gas giant's storm system fills the lower view, a hurricane eye larger than a continent staring upward, lightning flickering deep in the bands.
Beyond the canopy a crippled cruiser burns ahead, its midsection venting atmosphere in a long freezing plume, escape pods tumbling away into the dark around it.
Beyond the glass a wormhole terminus shimmers, its throat a perfect circle of distorted starlight, the stars behind it stretched into rings, something enormous emerging through it.
Beyond the canopy a desert world glows rust-red below, its terminator line crisp, a chain of impact craters catching long shadows in the low orbital light.
Beyond the glass a friendly fleet emerges from jump simultaneously — ships tearing back into normal space in sequence, each arrival a pulse of blue-white light.
Beyond the canopy a comet passes close, its nucleus dark and cratered, its twin tails — dust and ion — streaming away in different directions across the starfield.
Beyond the glass the galaxy core arches overhead, a dense river of light from edge to edge of the canopy, the cockpit interior faintly lit by ten billion suns.
